correctness.rationale: The simplicial vertices are the 4n directed arcs of bidirected K_{2,n}; subsets are admitted precisely when indegrees and outdegrees are ≤1 and no directed cycle occurs. Each face has ≤4 arcs. Independent enumeration gives all augmented face vectors for n=1..4; exact integral unit-incidence Schur cancellations give surviving reduced chain ranks for n=4 of eight degree-two generators and one degree-three generator with boundary coefficients −2,2,2. Its Smith divisor 2 yields Htilde_2=Z^7⊕Z/2 with no other n4 homology; previous n=1..3 groups match the claimed free homology. The arc-overlap graph of oriented four-cycles is connected, so Definition 4.2(b) of Caputi et al forces every nonempty dynamical region to contain all arcs; the connected whole graph meets the axioms and is the unique minimal module, and every vertex has positive in/out degree. Thus it is an unstable module. Independent standard-library integer cancellation reproduced face vectors (1,16,80,144,72), pivot sequence (71,65,15,1) and residual divisor two. This is an exhaustive finite computation because the chain and all faces were enumerated.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS. Caputi–Collari–Di Trani–Smith state the conjecture that a multipath complex of a torsion-bearing dynamical module should be stable and calculate other orientations including alternating bipartite graphs; their complete-bipartite orientation is not bidirected K2,4. The new explicit integral 2-torsion in an unstable single module directly contradicts that conjecture, not merely a nearby special-case bound. Published bidirected polygon computations and directed-tree matching complexes are different digraph families. No prior exact bidirected K2,4 integral calculation was located in the queried literature or Resultary.
residual_risks: No classification is proved for larger n or arbitrary digraphs; minimality is only n≤4.
A coincident computation in an unindexed integral multipath-homology database cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The direct counterexample resolves a falsifiable structural conjecture and supplies the smallest torsion-bearing member among n≤4 of a natural directed complete-bipartite family. Integral torsion (not merely mod-two Betti ranks) is essential; its failure of stable-module necessity is a meaningful boundary.
